definition: Hosting one base model with many hot-swappable LoRA adapters in a single deployment (S-LoRA-style batching across adapters).
details: Hosting one base model with many hot-swappable LoRA adapters in a single deployment (S-LoRA-style batching across adapters). The economics behind per-tenant and per-task customization without per-customer GPU fleets.

explainer.lead: Multi-LoRA serving lets one base model host many hot-swappable LoRA adapters in a single deployment. It makes per-tenant and per-task customization economical without provisioning a separate GPU fleet for every customer.

tiers.eli5: It's like one kitchen cooking many different recipes by swapping small spice kits, instead of building a whole separate kitchen for each dish.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers batch requests across adapters in a single deployment, S-LoRA-style, so many tenants share one base model. A common pitfall is uneven adapter traffic, which complicates batching and memory planning.
tiers.paperLevel: One shared base model is combined with many LoRA adapters that can be swapped at serving time, with batching performed across adapters in the same deployment.

explainer.example: A SaaS platform serves many customers from one base model, loading each customer's LoRA adapter on demand rather than running a dedicated GPU fleet per customer.
